title: EU-China
gist: MERICS EU-China hub page (mostly a listing of publications, staff and events); the only substantive content is a podcast blurb on the new MERICS Europe-China Resilience Audit, a 98-indicator index covering economy, security, politics and society.

insights.claim: MERICS has launched a Europe-China Resilience Audit built on a database of 98 indicators spanning economy, security, politics and society to measure Europe's ability to manage China risks.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A structured, indicator-based gauge of European exposure to China that could inform derisking policy and sector exposure screening.
insights.quote: we recently launched the MERICS Europe-China Resilience Audit, which is based on a database of 98 indicators for the economy, security, politics and society

insights.claim: MERICS frames resilience, defined as managing risks without compromising long-term development, as the core of Europe's adjustment of its China policy.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Signals that European China policy is being organized around managed derisking rather than decoupling.
insights.quote: Building resilience, i.e., the ability to manage risks without compromising long-term development, is at the heart of Europe’s adjustment of its China policy.

insights.claim: MERICS executive director Mikko Huotari argues even VW's best-case scenario in China involves immense costs, and that Europe needs to wean itself off the 'China drug'.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Flags structural downside for European automakers' China exposure even in optimistic scenarios.
insights.quote: There is still a best-case scenario for VW—but even that “involves immense costs” (Welt)
